00238.publication: Van Cutsem et al. J Clin Oncol 2012;30:3499–3506
00238.population: Patients with metastatic colorectal cancer previously treated with oxaliplatin; prior bevacizumab was permitted
00238.arms: Aflibercept 4mg/kg + FOLFIRI (n=612) versus placebo + FOLFIRI (n=614), every 2 weeks
limitations: Second-line metastatic oxaliplatin-exposed population; do not apply to adjuvant disease or all CRC patients.
Median survival difference is a group comparison, not the extra lifetime an individual patient can expect.
Added VEGF-inhibition toxicity and enhanced chemotherapy-associated toxicity; benefit must be weighed against fitness and treatment burden.
Primary OS confidence interval was 95.34%, not 95%.

00791.source_cited_by_nccp: Sasaki et al. 2013 Annals of Oncology conference abstract P-0210
00791.design: Single-arm phase II study of an entire stop-and-go treatment strategy
00791.sequence: Bevacizumab plus mFOLFOX6 for six cycles, then bevacizumab plus simplified LV5FU2 for twelve cycles, with subsequent oxaliplatin reintroduction
limitations: The study evaluates induction, maintenance and reintroduction as a whole, not isolated bevacizumab/5-FU/folinic acid.
No randomised comparator for the isolated 00791 regimen; do not attach the strategy survival or response numbers as this maintenance regimen's quantified benefit.
NCCP also cites OPTIMOX1, which evaluates an oxaliplatin stop-and-go strategy and is not proof of a specific isolated bevacizumab maintenance survival gain.
NCCP00791v2 explicitly identifies bevacizumab use in this regimen as unlicensed in Ireland and requires informed consent/local governance.
